subject: Provisional Net90 + Escrow / Phased Prepay for Clarion Health
messages:
From: Ryan Patel <ryan@clarionhealth.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: Clarion Health Finance <ap@clarionhealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick ask: temporary quarterly + deposit structure?

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Clarion is excited about the latency/cost numbers. Finance is asking whether we can pilot a slightly different payment pattern while they sort year-end cashflows. Our ask: 1) a 6-month pilot where we pay quarterly instead of monthly, and 2) push to Net-90 on invoices during the pilot, BUT we are willing to put a 25% upfront deposit into an escrow account and sign a PO.

They provided a PO stub (attached). Can Redwood approve this structure for pilot customers, or do you need exec signoff? We don’t want to slow the onboarding.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call.

— Ryan
Director, Cloud Integrations
Clarion Health

Attachments: Clarion_PO_7842.pdf (pdf)

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Ryan Patel <ryan@clarionhealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-02T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask: temporary quarterly + deposit structure?

Ryan — appreciate the clear proposal and for attaching the PO. Internal team looped in. Quick answers up front: we can do a pilot with a modified billing cadence provided we (a) receive a 25% escrow deposit up front, (b) have a signed PO and DocuSign addendum that clarifies the pilot window and termination rights, and (c) Finance & Legal sign off.

Laura — can you run a quick risk calc on a 6-month Net-90 pilot with the 25% deposit? If the numbers look ok I’ll escalate for exec approval (we typically require at least partial prepay for extended invoice terms).

Marissa — please advise on the minimum contract language we need to add to protect Redwood (escrow release triggers, service-level reclaim on nonpayment).

Jonas / Grace — heads up that this is likely a strategic pilot (large account, potential expansion). If we proceed, Sales wants a short mutual action plan so the customer isn’t held up.

I’ll pull this together for an exec note if Finance/Legal are comfortable.

— Rishi
Senior Director, Deal Desk
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-03T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask: temporary quarterly + deposit structure? — Finance view

Rishi — did a short model. Notes:

- Customer ARR in ask is modest (~$120k ARR) but has upsell potential.
- With a 25% upfront escrow (equivalent to ~1.5 months coverage), our exposure under Net-90 for a 6-month pilot looks tolerable if we tighten release conditions.
- Recommended guardrails: (1) escrow holds 25% of signed 6-month committed spend and releases on a 45/90 schedule tied to invoice payment, (2) we require a PO and a payment plan in DocuSign, (3) if customer misses >1 invoice beyond Net-90 during pilot, Redwood can suspend service and retain escrow for unrecovered usage.

I can approve subject to Legal drafting the addendum and Exec sign-off on the temporary terms (we treat this as a credit exception).

Laura
Head of Finance Operations
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-03T13:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask: temporary quarterly + deposit structure? — Legal addendum

Rishi/Laura — draft guidance and the attachment (proposed_escrow_term_sheet.xlsx) attached. Key points I plan to include in the addendum:

1) Definitions: pilot period (6 months), escrow amount (25% of committed pilot spend), release schedule (50% after first quarterly invoice cleared, remainder on final settlement)
2) Remedies: Redwood may suspend service for non-payment after a 7-day cure period; escrow may be applied to outstanding invoices after a 14-day cure on final demand.
3) Termination: Either party can terminate pilot with 30 days' notice; on termination Redwood will reconcile usage and return any remaining escrow within 30 days less any applied amounts.
4) No precedent clause: this pilot addendum is non-precedential and expires with the pilot.

I will prepare a short addendum and a single-sentence exec approval memo describing the exception and our risk mitigations. Please confirm acceptance of the terms below so I can prepare the DocuSign packet.

— Marissa
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed_escrow_term_sheet.xlsx (xlsx)

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: board-exec-approvals@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-04T15:38:00-07:00
Subject: Exec approval request — Clarion Health temporary billing exception (Net-90 with 25% escrow prepay)

Team — requesting an expedited Exec sign-off for a temporary billing exception for Clarion Health (Deal CLAR-2027-0421). Summary below:

Customer: Clarion Health (healthcare data SaaS integrator)
Proposal: 6-month pilot; Redwood invoices quarterly but permits Net-90 payment terms during pilot. Customer will deposit 25% of the 6-month committed spend into an escrow account before onboarding. PO received (attached).
Risk mitigation already approved by Finance & Legal:
- Finance: tolerable exposure with escrow; recommended release schedule and suspension rights.
- Legal: addendum drafted with suspension, escrow application, and non-precedent clause.

Decision requested: Exec sign-off to allow Sales to send DocuSign addendum and to provision service pending receipt of escrow.

If approved, please reply all with "APPROVE: Clarion pilot". If you need changes I’ll coordinate urgent call. We’d like to finalize by EOD Friday to keep onboarding momentum.

Thanks — Rishi
Senior Director, Deal Desk
Redwood Inference
summary: Customer asked for a 6-month pilot with quarterly invoicing and Net-90; proposed 25% escrow prepay. Finance and Legal recommend with guardrails; Rishi escalated to execs for approval.
